# SK0282 — The record writes out the property its parameter generates

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A property in a record body that restates, initializer included, the one its positional parameter already generates.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Cleanup |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

`record Point(int X, int Y) { public int X { get; init; } = X; }` writes out character for character what the positional parameter already produces, and it costs a reader the same question every time: is this one different? ⚠ It belongs disproportionately to generated code — "declare the properties" is what most of a model's training data does, and the positional record is newer than most of that data, so the two forms arrive together.

⚠ **Not hosted, measured the same way as `SK0280` and `SK0281`**: absent from all 442 descriptors read out of SDK 10.0.400's analyzer assemblies, and silent in a probe with all 120 `IDE` ids and all 320 `CA` ids at `warning` on a compilation where `IDE0055`, `IDE0160`, `IDE0290`, `IDE0380` and `CA1051` fired and no analyzer crashed. `jb inspectcode` 2025.2.6 reports it on the same file.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
record Point(int X, int Y) {
    public int X { get; init; } = X;
}
```

Write:

```csharp
record Point(int X, int Y);
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **Which accessor pair is generated depends on the record kind, and getting it wrong deletes a property that was doing something.** A `record class` and a `readonly record struct` generate `{ get; init; }`; a mutable `record struct` generates `{ get; set; }`. So `{ get; init; }` written on a mutable record struct is *not* redundant — it makes the property init-only, which the generated one is not — and it is declined. ⚠ **The initializer must be present and must be the parameter itself, asked of the symbol rather than of the spelling.** A hand-written positional property with no `= X` is not assigned by the generated constructor at all, so deleting it changes what the record stores; and `= X` binding to anything other than the primary constructor's parameter is a different program. ⚠ **An attribute, an accessor modifier, an accessor body, an expression body, a non-`public` or extra modifier, or a parameter carrying a default or an attribute all withdraw the finding**: the generated property has none of those, so anything written there is the author's. ⚠ The whole declaration is deleted with its leading trivia, so a documentation comment on it is a reason to leave it alone rather than something to remove.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK0282.severity`
